resources.string: Add an information card to your photos. Select up to %1$d photos; swipe to edit each one, then save all.
100% uses the reference text size. Enlarging text keeps the card width.
JPEG, HEIC and AVIF can retain HDR gain maps. Video and portrait data require compatible output formats.
The information card is too tall. Reduce its size or shorten the text, then save again.
There is not enough memory to process this photo. Close other apps and try again, or choose a smaller photo.
The portrait depth data could not be preserved during export. Try keeping location and capture time enabled in the save options, or turn off Apple portrait conversion.
Used when an imported photo has no photographer. Individual photo edits do not change this default.
Save and apply to current photo
Uses photo GPS to look up the city and country, usually in English. This may send coordinates to the system location service; the photo and your current location are not shared.
Optional. Used when no lens profile matches a new photo. Leave blank if unknown.
Enter a number from 1 to 200, or leave blank.
Uses the photo GPS, not your current location.
Camera access is needed to identify this device’s lenses. No photos are taken. You can also add a lens manually.
Lens details could not be read. Try again or add a lens manually.
Some characteristics could not be read. This is not a complete hardware inventory.
Use a product name for display and the photo’s EXIF model to match photos.
This container cannot yet be exported with all auxiliary data intact. The original stays unchanged; export is blocked instead of flattening it.
Preserving this Ultra HDR image requires Android 14 or later.
Use JPEG to preserve the HDR gainmap or Motion Photo video. PNG cannot contain these parts.
The platform could not decode the HDR gainmap. Export stopped to prevent HDR loss.
The encoded HDR data failed verification. No result was published.
The exported media container failed verification. No result was published.
Edit a photo information card, match saved lens profiles, and preserve supported Ultra HDR and Motion Photo data.
Scan visible lenses or edit names, ranges and zoom mappings.
Lens removed. Save profiles to keep this change.
Add a lens profile to fill missing lens names and magnification when you import photos.
For a fixed lens, use the same native focal length at both ends. Digital crops have separate coverage rules.
Optional zoom at each native focal endpoint. A fixed lens uses equal values; for example, 1 and 1.
Optional actual focal lengths from Camera2 or EXIF, not 35mm-equivalent values. Leave blank if unknown.
Enter product name, EXIF model, lens name and valid native ranges. Optional ranges need both endpoints.
The upper value must not be smaller than the lower value.
Enter a positive number no greater than %1$d.
Changes on this page have not been saved. Discard them and return?
Open photos and unsaved edits will be cleared. Any ongoing save will stop; photos already saved remain in your gallery.
Select up to %1$d photos at a time.
Each of the %1$d photos keeps its original pixel dimensions.
Use the model recorded in the original photo. This may differ from the product name.
Optional limit for focal-length matching. If blank, coverage extends toward the next lens on the same device. Actual physical lens metadata takes priority.
Enter a value between the native maximum zoom and 200; fill both native zoom endpoints first.
All detected lenses are configured. Edit them in the list below.
Multiple profiles use the same hardware lens ID. Remove duplicate bindings before saving.
Fixed native focal length needs equal native zoom endpoints. Enter digital coverage in the field below.
Device, lens and exposure details. Location and time are separate; video device metadata follows this choice.
The photo could not be read. Download the original to this device, then choose it from Files.
The photo could not be saved. Check free storage and folder access, then save again. Your original is unchanged.
This font could not be opened. Choose another TTF or OTF file. Your current font is unchanged.
The preview could not be generated. Reopen the original photo and try again.
Access was denied. Choose the file again and allow access when prompted.
Camera access is off. Allow it in app settings to find lenses, or add a lens manually.
Apply these changes, then save the profiles on the previous page.
Opening new photos discards unsaved photo or settings edits. Exported photos are unaffected.
Opening %1$d new photo discards unsaved edits. Saved photos are unaffected.
Opening %1$d new photos discards unsaved edits. Saved photos are unaffected.
HEIC keeps the HDR gain map when present. Encoding support depends on your device.
HEIC export requires Android 9 or later.
SF Compact Rounded Medium + SF Mono Medium
Retain original photo/video location, or remove it when off. Visible card text is unchanged.
Retain photo capture dates and video creation times. Turn off to omit the original capture time.
Used for each save. Temporary changes apply only to that save.
These choices apply to this save only, without changing defaults.
This video container cannot be safely cleaned. Adjust save options or use a supported original Motion Photo.
No app could open this photo, or read access expired. Open it from your gallery.
Could not open the share menu. Share the saved photo from your gallery.
Cannot read shared content. Share 1–50 images from your gallery, or select the originals in the app.
This video could not be played. Check that the original is complete and its codec is supported. You can continue editing the photo.
AVIF export needs Android 14 or later and an AV1 encoder.
Save a paired photo and MOV to a folder. Transfer both files together to import as a Live Photo.
Choose JPEG or HEIC and a destination folder for the Live Photo pair.
Convert Xiaomi portrait to Apple depth
Tags the HEIC export with an identity (Standard) photographic style so Apple devices show the style controls.
Adds the texture-style metadata and part mattes that unlock the texture / film grain / glow controls in Apple Photos; automatically includes the plain photographic style.
Photographic style metadata requires HEIC format.
Motion photos are recognized by Android galleries only in JPEG exports; Apple devices need the paired Live Photo output.
Use the unblurred image, relative depth and portrait mask. Save as HEIC for depth editing on Apple devices.
Choose HEIC to include Apple portrait depth.
Choose AVIF or HEIC to preserve this photo’s 10-bit color and dynamic range.
This device has no encoder for the selected format. Choose another supported format.
These photos need different output formats. Save the 10-bit AVIF photos separately from Motion Photos and portraits.
Camera or phone product name. Blank fields stay hidden.
Lens name read from the photo or matched to a saved profile.
Resolution in megapixels, not file size.
35 mm-equivalent focal length and optional zoom ratio.
ISO sensitivity recorded by the camera.
Adjust background opacity; text stays opaque.
Blur photo details behind the card.
Distance from the photo edge, scaled with the photo.
The photo could not be prepared for export. Reopen the original and try again.
The photographic style layer could not be written into the HEIC file. The original is unchanged.
The portrait depth could not be decoded or aligned. The original is unchanged.
The video could not be prepared with these metadata options.
The full-resolution photo could not be decoded. The original is unchanged.
The device could not encode this image with its HDR data. Try another supported format.
The encoded image did not retain the required color or HDR data, so it was not saved.
The device could not encode the portrait depth and matte into HEIC. The original is unchanged.
The image was created but could not be written to the gallery or selected folder.
There is not enough free storage to save this photo.
The photo map module is reserved and will arrive in a later update.
Choose a local font for this card. The reference typeface is restored when you reset it.
